title: My childhood in Chiyyaram — comic adaptation (Chapter 1)
style: Hand-painted watercolour-and-gouache animation-background style. Soft natural light, lush green 1950s Kerala countryside, warm gentle palette, clean expressive character linework, cinematic composition, whimsical but grounded, suitable for young children. Absolutely no text, letters, captions, signage or speech bubbles anywhere in the image.

valiyammavan.role: a tall, dignified feudal landlord (janmi) of 1950s Kerala in his 50s: a round face with full cheeks, a prosperous, well-fed build with a slight paunch, short closely cropped thinning grey hair (not bald), completely clean-shaven (no beard, no moustache), kadukkan: small, short, thin U-shaped gold-wire earrings hanging just below each earlobe, close to the ear (not studs on the side of the lobe), with a tiny red stone in the centre of the U, ONLY on his RIGHT wrist a medium-thick gold bracelet whose two ends meet at a tiny, discreet gold elassu joint (his LEFT wrist is always bare): a long white mundu worn straight down to the ankles with a thin dark border, and a white melmundu resting over one shoulder (not across the chest), bare-chested at home, calm and kind face
valiyammavan.photoNote: OPTIONAL: a photo of Govinda Menon at refs/valiyammavan.jpg. Without one, he is drawn from this placeholder description; ask Achan.

achachan_today.role: a warm Kerala grandfather around 80 years old, today: lean face, short white hair, thick white moustache drooping at the corners, white chin stubble, rectangular dark-framed glasses, modern clothes (polo shirts, checked shirts, jeans), often a straw fedora when out

panels.scene: Present day, evening, inside a modern Kerala home. The older brother and little sister lie on their stomachs on a cool tiled floor beside a stack of handwritten pages in Malayalam script and an old fountain pen, warm lamp light, the brother reading aloud and the sister leaning in eagerly.

Same room. Glowing ink-like ribbons of golden light rise from the handwritten pages and swirl around the two amazed children like fireflies; a magical wind lifts their hair; the room begins to dissolve into green light.

Wide establishing shot. The two children, small in the frame, stand on a narrow raised ridge between flooded green paddy fields in a 1950s Kerala village at misty sunrise. Coconut palms line the horizon, egrets in the field, a small distant temple lamp glowing.

On the paddy-field ridge, the 1950s village boy has run up and stopped short, staring curiously at the two children's strange modern clothes. The older brother looks at him in dawning wonder; the little sister hides half behind her brother.

Seen from behind, the village boy leads the two children up the long, flat, unpaved red-earth pathway towards the ancestral home (Korappath Kalappurakkal), pointing ahead, between jackfruit trees, palms and garden land, early 1950s. Ahead of them stands the padippura gatehouse: a wide single-storey building under one broad tiled roof, an arched passage with a dark wooden door frame, storage rooms with barred windows on both sides. The house lies behind and slightly below it: only its long tiled roof and the small attic room show. Thatched barn to the right.

The wide wooden veranda of the ancestral home, 1950s. Several village men and women in simple traditional Kerala clothing sit and stand quietly waiting their turn. The three children peek around a wooden pillar; the little sister looks puzzled.

On the veranda, the dignified older man sits calmly on a wooden chair, listening patiently to two village farmers who are both talking and gesturing at once. The three children watch from behind a pillar in the background. Do not show any objects that suggest what the problem is about.

The two farmers, now smiling, shake hands. One farmer offers a bunch of bananas to the dignified older man, who gently raises his palm and pushes it back with a kind smile, refusing. In the foreground the little sister's mouth is open in surprise; her brother smiles.

Morning. Seen from behind, the three children stand on the house's red-oxide verandah between two carved black-painted wooden pillars, watching the dignified older man, in crisp white clothes with a black umbrella, walk away across the long flat red-earth yard towards the padippura gatehouse: one building under one tiled roof, with a covered platform on wooden pillars and five red-oxide steps up to the archway, on his way to town.

Wide panorama from a raised field ridge: the three children, seen from behind and small in frame, look out over vast green paddy fields, coconut groves and a few farm workers in the fields, golden afternoon light, 1950s Kerala.

Sunset on the paddy-field ridge. Golden ink-like ribbons of light begin to swirl around the two modern children again. The little sister presses a small sweet into the village boy's hand; he looks puzzled but waves goodbye. The older brother waves too.

Present day, evening, a modern Kerala home. The grandfather sits at a small desk writing on handwritten pages with a fountain pen. The two children have just burst in excitedly, the brother mid-sentence; the grandfather looks up over his reading glasses and smiles warmly.
